description: Same universe, folds, costs, sizing, gates and incumbent as v2/v4/v5, and the same leaf vocabulary as v5. ONE change, and it is a correction rather than a widening: warmup_bars goes from 600 to 2100 so that every leaf and every family parameter is fully warm at the START of each fold. Under 600 bars a rule whose lookback exceeded the warm-up was undefined for the opening stretch of every fold - up to 27% of a two-year fold at a 1800-bar window - so its measured performance depended on its own parameter rather than on the market. Numbers for long-lookback families are therefore NOT comparable with v2/v4/v5; the incumbent's are, and were verified unchanged.

incumbent.description: Current research incumbent; not an automatic deployment recommendation.

notes: preferred_sequence is only a tie-break order now; every compatible family the binary lists is schedulable
ensemble_ls is excluded because it requires --long-short while this mission evaluates long-only portfolios
quotas are measured over the last quota_window recorded candidates; the mode furthest below its share is scheduled

a family is saturated when >= min_evaluations were scored and the best over all did not beat the best before the last window by min_improvement; it then gets one drift check every drift_every candidates
near_duplicate_distance is the L-infinity distance between parameter vectors normalised to [0,1] over each legal range
measured 2026-09-06 on the v2 ledger: 151 tsmom parameter sets with best +0.27, indistinguishable from the best of 106 coin-flip controls (+0.26); 25 of 35 families never scheduled

v5: memory_order_* is a regime gate, not an entry trigger. It is causal (window [i-w+1, i]), reads the median order over three small radii because spiral.h is explicit that one radius is not a measurement, and refits every max(10, window/40) bars on a DERIVED cadence so it adds no searchable knob. The earlier manual test of this idea (cli_trader/experiments/order_gate) ranked instruments on full-sample spectra and is explicitly not tradeable; this leaf tests the weaker causal claim instead.

measured before adding it: alpha runs about -0.8..+1.1 on 4h crypto with a median near -0.2, i.e. in the fractional band -1 < alpha < 0; the threshold range [-1.5,1.0] brackets that and the window floor of 300 bars is what the estimator needs to see a power-law tail at all

v6 measurement, 4 protocol coins, warm-up 600 vs 2100: the incumbent is IDENTICAL in every fold (0.09 / 2.22 / 0.29), and so is tsmom - anything warm within 600 bars is unaffected, so the comparison baseline is stable. What moves is exactly what should: vr_switch at vrWindow=800 loses 0.06 and 0.23 Sharpe in the two folds checked, vol_managed at rankWindow=750 loses 0.02 and 0.09. Those two were being flattered by sitting out the opening of each fold. This flaw predates the memory_order leaf; the leaf only made it visible.

v6 also removes a prompt artifact: v5 told the model the memory_order window 'MUST BE 300-2000 bars, far longer than the other leaves', and the model duly picked a median of 1200, which under the 600-bar warm-up blinded the leaf for a fifth of every fold. Measured zero-trade rate by window under v5: 0% at 300-600, 33% at 1001-1500, 42% at 1501-2000, against 10% for specs without the leaf. The prompt now states what the window actually controls - regime cadence, about 35-day regimes at 500 bars and about 100-day at 1500 - instead of urging length for its own sake.

checked before adopting: a 2100-bar warm-up reaches back to 2017-01-16 from the first fold, which stays clear of the thin carried-forward XRP/LTC bars of 2015-16 that inflate any statistic read across them.
